## App Lock privacy repair and scoped release preparation — 2026-10-25

PR 1109 originally withheld full-page children and moved PIN checking to a rate-limited action, but still stored the salt/hash in authenticated-readable and writable `user_preferences.notification_prefs.appLock`. That allowed offline guessing and direct replacement/removal of the lock. Independent review also reproduced unlock-cookie reuse across new login sessions, a settings compare-and-set authorization race, and onboarding reset/finalize replacing an existing PIN. These are confirmed defects; the earlier layout-only change is not accepted as a complete privacy repair.

The integrated candidate moves credentials to `app_lock_credentials`, with explicit browser-role privilege revocation and deny-all RLS. The atomic migration preserves valid existing enabled and disabled PINs, rejects malformed legacy records, removes the public JSON key, and rejects its reintroduction. Settings exposes only status; PIN creation and verification stay on the server. Credential writes compare the exact authorized revision, onboarding only seeds an absent private record, and browser unlocks bind to the verified Auth session, private revision and a 12-hour server expiry. Lock now rotates the revision. The layout checks privacy before household/billing props; a separate request guard provides defense in depth for protected page and partial-RSC requests before Next chooses a subtree. The real Next 16.4.2 retained-layout control reproduced the response leak: after removing the unlock cookie, sibling navigation returned HTTP 200 Flight (3,049 bytes) containing the protected leaf sentinel. With the request guard, the same navigation redirected with no leaf; locked document/RSC/action-POST and storage/Auth outage cases also remained closed. The earlier unavailable-CDP-body observation was a capture failure, not a valid negative control. The retained proof is `scripts/verify-app-lock-rsc.mjs` (local synthetic Auth/DB seams, actual Next/browser transport). Direct API/native access remains governed by Supabase authentication and RLS; App Lock is a web privacy screen, not a replacement authorization boundary.

It was audited at base `8b35245e9` (land/q5: main `99cf18b4d` plus the coverage sweep's follow-up rounds, which have since merged as #1087) and lands on main `b2bfa3a27`. Four lenses (bounds, gates, public, seeds) produced 23 candidates (5, 4, 9 and 5); the top 20 were each checked by two skeptical verifiers: 19 confirmed (N1 to N19), 0 disputed, 1 refuted. The refuted candidate said every published testimonial and case study is labelled "Shared with permission" while nothing records that permission; both verifiers found that the only writer is the stepped-up super-admin whose Publish tick is the business's attestation, and that a consent column would be filled in by the same operator, so it is a copy or process note, not a code defect. The three candidates beyond the top 20 were not verified in this run: a third copy of the model-map finding (N14), the `/admin/ai` model never reaching the planner, structured calls or vision while "Test connection" reports it, and the model allow-list matching by prefix, so an unknown id that starts with an allowed one passes as capable. The verifiers merged five duplicate groups (N3 and N7 into N1, N10 into N5, N11 into N4, N13 into N8, N15 into N14) and narrowed several findings: the two seeds do harm only once an operator runs the shown SQL, and their pages' missing step-up and client-chunk SQL reach nothing on their own; the referral cap is an operator-error amplifier for a stepped-up super-admin, and the credits offset invoices rather than pay cash; N6 holds under the AUD16-16 threat model only; the marketplace seed's oldest-family fallback fires only where the hard-coded address has no family, since in production it resolves to the owner's anchor family. ## Merge and production preflight — 2026-10-04 00:26 UTC, Codex/root

GitHub refresh: 110 open PRs, 109 drafts; 49 target `main`, 61 target other PR branches, and nine are `DIRTY`/conflicting. The only non-draft is #834, based on `main`; it is `DIRTY`, with required Typecheck/Lint/Test/Build, Mobile, and Database jobs failed while E2E passes. Do not merge the batch or promote a draft as release-ready. The current Vercel CLI `whoami` attempt exits with `unable to verify the first certificate`, and this audit checkout has no Vercel project link. Production deployment status therefore cannot be confirmed or safely changed from this environment.

Exact-head #918 review (head `3d0c49cc0473d5cf43870d9040570c4f69a9cdee`, stacked on #913) found four release-blocking gaps. The family boundary is source-derived: an authenticated owner can write an arbitrary `sync_external_mappings.local_id`, and service-role folding reads/updates the target event by ID without family/calendar scope; the two-family database repro was not run. Changed-master-only pulls can overwrite previously folded exception slots. Overlapping syncs can lose disjoint slots through read-merge-write without serialization. String Set dedupe treats equal instants such as `...+00:00` and `....000Z` as different; JS equality behavior was checked, but a PostgREST round-trip was not. Current fake/in-memory tests and migration SQL probe do not cover these paths. Keep #918 unmerged until family-scoped reads/writes, durable date reconciliation, concurrency control, and timestamp normalization have executable coverage.

Isolated #890 commit `7a951926c0908abcd64bb50b4928c60a343c3b8a` is on exact PR head `610c4235f2f3e6bb67adaa31245576a70c6097b8`; synthetic PG17 fresh migration/runtime and both cleanup/adoption orderings pass, as do focused tests (6 files/99 tests), 8 GB TypeScript, migration audit, and diff checks. - Independent meal review (2026-10-03 15:07 UTC): On exact #897 head `084d1353`, `planWeek` writes created meals to the shared library before the atomic planning RPC and deletes them if a later entry fails resolution. A concurrent successful plan can start referencing one of those meals before the first request's cleanup deletes it; `meal_plans.meal_id` has `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so the committed plan silently loses its meal reference. Request-ID validation also occurs after library writes. AutoPlan UI/route pass no stable request key, while service fallback generates a new UUID, so a retry after commit with a lost HTTP reply can replace the week again. The test called “lost RPC response” asserts there were no plan table writes and does not cover commit-then-lost-response. Current exact-head #897 checks: Database and meal-plan SQL pass, Main fails, Mobile passes, E2E pending; #890 Database, E2E and Main fail while meal-plan SQL and Mobile pass. Findings remain open; no new acceptance or audit credit.
- Independent follow-up (2026-10-03 15:08 UTC): Guardian SMS reliability finding remains reproducible in source: `app/api/guardian/escalate/route.ts` sends before persisting the aggregate result and swallows provider errors; callback recovery reclaims an error/stale processing row after 10 minutes, while completion-write errors are ignored. There is no per-recipient durable receipt, so accepted-but-unrecorded work may resend and a swallowed send failure may be marked processed without repair. Existing tests only fail before send or inspect source ordering; they do not exercise post-send persistence failure/unknown provider response. Exact family-scoped manager selection is intact; no new isolation leak found and no provider was called. Migration `0479_a_run_with_no_attempts_left_is_abandoned_not_reclaimed.sql:92–114,141–151` dead-letters an exhausted run; its step update excludes `awaiting_approval`, then it cancels only approvals still pending. Approval decisions separately CAS `pending`→`approved` (`lib/services/approvals/index.ts:283–295`); if that commits before cleanup, the approved row is skipped. Reproducible source ordering: an expired executing run at the attempt ceiling has an approval-gated step; the parent approval commits, cron marks the run failed but skips the awaiting step, then `foldIntoRun` changes that step to `ready` before its terminal-run guard returns (`approvals/index.ts:425–430,456–462`). It still returns `released: gated.length`; the linked tool approval caller treats that positive count as handled (`:761–770`). Result: approved request and ready step attached to a failed run, while the approved work never executes. The run itself is not reopened in this ordering. There is no transaction or cross-row guard coupling approval resolution to dead-letter state. The SQL probe and tests exercise sequential cases, not this concurrent ordering. Guard approval decisions/step writes against terminal runs or serialize resolution with dead-letter reconciliation, plus add a deterministic concurrent regression. This is source-interleaving analysis, not a DB race harness. Exact-head CI run [37142388498](https://github.com/NewWorldVenture/Bubaly/actions/runs/37142388498) passes Main, Database, E2E, Mobile, and Vercel checks; Supabase Preview skips. Green sequential CI does not establish this race. No branch, migration, production data/configuration, or closure status changed.

## #919 Outlook series mirror loses Graph-native cancelled occurrences — 2026-10-03 18:56 UTC, Codex/root

Read-only review of exact open head `e06647950a65ea207bc4d9d30f845c7f9d329b73` found two provider-contract gaps. First, `MsEvent` omits Graph's series-master `cancelledOccurrences`; `msEventToRow` always emits `exception_dates: []` and only folds separate `type:'exception'` rows (`lib/sync/providers/microsoft.ts:147–170,365–367`). A synthetic Graph-shaped weekly master carrying `cancelledOccurrences:['OID.<master>.2026-07-29']` therefore maps to a local RRULE with no skip date, recreating the cancelled occurrence. The PR's `CANCELLED` fixture is a separate cancelled exception event, not the documented master representation. Microsoft documents `cancelledOccurrences` as occurrence IDs on a series master ([Get event](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/event-get?view=graph-rest-1.0), [event resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/event?view=graph-rest-1.0)). Second, the importer requests `/me/calendars/{id}/events/delta` against Graph v1.0 (`microsoft.ts:203–216`); Microsoft's API docs say unbounded event delta is beta-only, while v1.0 supports bounded `calendarView/delta` and returns recurring occurrences/exceptions ([event delta v1.0](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/event-delta?view=graph-rest-1.0), [delta query guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/delta-query-events)). Tests currently mock the URL and payload; no real Graph call was made. Family scoping appears account-local (`account_id` plus provider) in the reviewed fold/write path. ## #903 card retry follow-up leaves the previously tracked provider-response gap open — 2026-10-03 18:54 UTC, Codex/root

Read-only review of exact open head `1494abb041c54c08b6f6e1ae5f712df01cc5e9fe` found that the current tests simulate a lost database insert reply after mirror commit, not a lost provider `cards.create` response. If Stripe creates the card but the response is lost, the mirror is never written and the same count-based key is retried; changed controls are refused as an idempotency-parameter mismatch, while a retry after Stripe prunes the key may create a second unlisted physical card. The webhook skips unmatched provider card IDs, so it does not reconcile the orphan. This is the same provider-unknown-outcome/key-expiry gap already recorded under #882, not a new audit item. No Stripe API call, money movement, or branch edit occurred. Stripe documents that keys may be pruned after at least 24 hours and reuse after pruning starts a new request: [Idempotent requests](https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests). No closure credit.

## Cron boundary bootstrap gap — 2026-10-03 16:33 UTC, Codex/root

On PR #902 exact head `ad19f27092bce3e5c625ccb986352ec5a6307e14`, the boundary lookup filters to successful scheduled runs, then treats an empty result as the first tick. The same empty response occurs if earlier scheduled runs exist but all failed or were cancelled, so a recovered tick can dispatch only its fixed five-minute window and finish green; if schedule deliveries were missed while no successful boundary existed, that tick becomes the next boundary and the gap is not recovered. The current empty-history tests do not distinguish first-ever execution from failed-only history because the API filter removes failures. This reproducible source/test gap was published at [#902](https://github.com/NewWorldVenture/Bubaly/pull/902#issuecomment-5971121597); requested a failed-only history regression and fail-closed boundary handling after dispatch. No branch changes. Current exact-head checks: Database, Mobile and Vercel pass; Main and E2E remain in progress; Supabase Preview skipped.

An independent reviewer confirmed the classification hole with synthetic scheduled `failure` and `cancelled` runs plus the current in-progress run: filtering the query to successful outcomes produces the same empty array as a true first run, which the code labels `lookup=ok`. The reviewer also found the `only this run` fixture labels its in-progress current run as successful; this does not invalidate the separate empty-array finding, but the fixture should be made realistic. GitHub REST documents the workflow-run status filter and conclusion values [here](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2026-03-10). No branch or ledger changes by the reviewer.

## Independent #890 race review — 2026-10-04 00:11 UTC, Codex/root

Independent read-only review found a second lifecycle race beyond same-name concurrent creation. In ordinary `planWeek`, `resolveEntries` may commit a new custom dish through `meal_ensure_custom` (`lib/services/meals/index.ts:318`) before all entries are resolved. If a later recipe lookup fails, `removeCreatedMeals` (`:481`) deletes that earlier meal. Between those operations, another writer can reuse the meal and commit its own `meal_plans` row; deleting the meal sets that other row's `meal_id` to NULL (`supabase/migrations/0002_tables.sql:229`). This can silently corrupt a successfully committed meal slot. Existing candidate concurrency proof races ordinary ensure against delegated replacement, not this failure-and-cleanup interleaving. The synthetic PG17 candidate's prior SQL/notes/rollback proof remains valid but does not cover this scenario. Root sent the exact interleaving to the isolated author; add a deterministic regression and ownership-safe cleanup before commit. Candidate author reports the 97/97 affected-suite run and 8GB typecheck still running. Original PR and production remain untouched; no completion credit is awarded.

- **TIME-003 finding: a title-only reminder edit moves the saved instant outside UTC (owner-account comment posted 2026-10-02 11:43 UTC, [#771 comment 5951639694](https://github.com/NewWorldVenture/Bubaly/pull/771#issuecomment-5951639694); read-only).**
  - **Mechanism, verified on main `01b2c380`:** the reminders-module blob is `296a2ec7`.
    - The edit field is filled with `reminder.remind_at.slice(0, 16)`, a UTC wall clock.
    - Save parses it with `new Date(remindAtRaw).toISOString()`, which reads it as device-local time.
  - **Reproduction:** the root's frozen receipt 0bf3f4 confirms author b45251. Each title-only Save shifts the instant by the device offset:
    - New York in October: 16:00Z → 20:00Z → 00:00Z the next day.
    - New York in December: 16:00Z → 21:00Z → 02:00Z the next day.
    - Tokyo: 16:00Z → 07:00Z → 22:00Z the previous day.
    - UTC does not drift. Cancel, an explicit refusal and a zero-row acknowledgment keep the original.
    - These are 7 characterization and control cases across 3 affected scenarios, not 7 workflow passes. This is a synthetic fixture; nothing about a deployed server, Auth, RLS or providers is claimed.
  - **Reconciliation with the NWV-held clock work:**
    - No held NWV work fixes this. The TIME-003 family-zone branches are already merged into main.
    - The stale `time003-wip-backup` changes only the reminder date *display* (`useFormat`), not the input conversion, and it is superseded.
    - Main already has the established pattern, `toLocalInput` / `fromLocalInput` from `lib/time/local-input` with the family zone, used by the calendar and behavior modules. The reminders form was not moved onto it.
    - NWV releases this one input consumer (the reminders `remind_at` fill and parse) to a root-authorized lane unless the owner says otherwise ([#771 comment 5951651650](https://github.com/NewWorldVenture/Bubaly/pull/771#issuecomment-5951651650)). The other TIME-003 consumers stay as recorded.
  - **Status:** `COMPONENT-8DAC200BDFEA` and MOD-083 stay **IN PROGRESS**, and the full edit and timezone workflow stays open. No PASS. **PRODUCTION READY: NO.**

This confirms deployed source identity, not application of the recorded owner SQL or whole native RLS acceptance.** The lane audited the two RLS rewrites no earlier lane recorded: migration 0481 (`supabase/migrations/0481_the_rls_sweep_narrows_the_household_tables_to_their_roles.sql`), which narrows the household tables' policies to each role and adds guest read guards and restrictive write guards, and the circle-management functions of 0483 (`supabase/migrations/0483_a_live_hold_counts_and_an_order_names_both_families.sql`: removal, block, leave, negotiation respond and auction close), for writes the database admits that the app never offers, writes the app offers that the database refuses, and screens that misstate rows RLS now withholds. 0490 (the calendar feed functions) is left to Codex, who maintains it and `lib/server/calendar-feeds.ts`; the critic's ask, a review of `calendar_feed_archive_sources` before release, stays with them. The lane was audited at main `99cf18b4d` and lands on main `1505e4285`, in the same PR as admin-reach round 7. Five lenses (sensitive reads, over-narrow writes, guards and guest triggers, circle RPCs, and how the app handles refusals) produced 17 candidates (3, 2, 2, 4 and 6); each was checked by two skeptical verifiers, each probing a private Postgres copy of main's migrations as the role in question: 15 confirmed (N1 to N15), 1 disputed, 1 refuted. N11 is N10 found by a second lens (the same nutrition route, policy and outcome). The verifiers narrowed several findings: N1's second half, that only a manager may dose a family-wide medicine, reverses 0481's [FIX 1] note ('dosed by whoever takes it') and is an owner decision, not a defect; N1, N2, N3 and N5 to N7 need a direct PostgREST or /rpc call (the module never offers the dose writes, and removal and block have no app caller, though leaving a circle does); N4 fails closed with an honest error and a clean rollback; N8, N9, N13 and N15 are display only, with no data exposed. The disputed candidate said a child can file a `chore_submissions` row naming any family chore, since 0481's guard pins `chore_id` only on update, and the parent's Approve card then shows and pays the planted chore; both verifiers reproduced the insert, one found it real, and the other found that it grants nothing the child lacks, since `chore_assignments_insert` lets a child self-assign the costlier chore (0464 records member writes on chores as consistent-open by design, ROLE-SCOPE-001) and a parent still decides on the non-auto path; it is recorded here and not fixed. The refuted candidate said a block bars only the family row, so a parent of the blocked family who manages another household rejoins with the old code while rotation has no app caller; both verifiers found that the block is per household by design (0483's own comment), that the other household joins under its own name and can be removed and blocked in turn, that a join code is a bearer secret, and that no app code calls removal, unblock or rotation, so an owner who can block through /rpc can rotate the same way. ## Admin actions that reach families or the public site — audit lane, PR #1088 — 2026-10-23

Result: **18 🛠 FIXED + PASS (ADMIN-01 to ADMIN-19 apart from ADMIN-06; N1, N3 and N7 share one fix, as do N4 and N11, N5 and N10, N8 and N13, and N14 and N15), 16 🛠 FIXED + PASS from review rounds 2 to 7 and the merged tree (ADMIN-R1 and ADMIN-R2, the two bridge P3s review round 1 raised; ADMIN-R3 to ADMIN-R5, the P1 and two P2s the round-2 fix introduced when the marketing cron's regeneration stripped the ownership marker, closed by its re-fix; ADMIN-R6 to ADMIN-R13 from rounds 3 to 6: the deploy-order item and the console-move P3 the second review of round 2 raised, the first taken by round 3 as a P2, the former-slug P3 the round-3 review raised, the regeneration race, the two job-runner P3s that exist on main, the stale embedding chunks, and the P2 the round-6 fix introduced, closed by its re-fix; ADMIN-R14 and ADMIN-R15, the two pre-existing overlapping-cron P3s the second review of round 6 raised, closed by round 7 in PR #1089; ADMIN-R16, a test-only conflict between round 7 and #1084 that PR #1089's merged-tree validation found and `7d1246236` fixed), 13 🔄 IN PROGRESS (ADMIN-06, the database step-up guard, which has no app-side fix; ADMIN-O1 to ADMIN-O11, the owner SQL, reviews and decisions; ADMIN-O14, a pre-existing P3 the round-7 review raised, recorded as a follow-up when the lane closed; ADMIN-O12 and ADMIN-O13, since fixed in ADMIN-R14 and ADMIN-R15 (PR #1089) and not counted; since round 3 the deploy no longer waits for ADMIN-O11, the mirror repair). Merged to main as `665c982d8` on 2026-10-23 at 18:55 UTC after a green run of all 16 checks that ran on `6817a08c1` (Supabase Preview skipped); www.bubaly.com/api/build-info served `665c982d8` at 19:00 UTC on 2026-10-23.** The lane audited super-admin actions that reach families or the public site and that no earlier lane owns: the referral settings and the reward path (`app/(app)/admin/marketing/referrals/actions.ts`, `lib/referrals/core.ts`, `lib/referrals/server.ts`), the knowledge-base seed page and its SQL, the admin marketing writers (exit intent, personalization, platform, reputation, AEO and landing pages) and what they publish under `p/[slug]`, `lp/[slug]` and the marketing pages, and the per-task model map in `lib/ai/routing.ts`, for who may call each, what bounds the input, whether the write is confirmed and audited, whether one operator mistake reaches every family or the public, and whether the public render is safe. It was audited at base `8b35245e9` (land/q5: main `99cf18b4d` plus the coverage sweep's follow-up rounds, which have since merged as #1087) and lands on main `b2bfa3a27`. Four lenses (bounds, gates, public, seeds) produced 23 candidates (5, 4, 9 and 5); the top 20 were each checked by two skeptical verifiers: 19 confirmed (N1 to N19), 0 disputed, 1 refuted. The refuted candidate said every published testimonial and case study is labelled "Shared with permission" while nothing records that permission; both verifiers found that the only writer is the stepped-up super-admin whose Publish tick is the business's attestation, and that a consent column would be filled in by the same operator, so it is a copy or process note, not a code defect. The three candidates beyond the top 20 were not verified in this run: a third copy of the model-map finding (N14), the `/admin/ai` model never reaching the planner, structured calls or vision while "Test connection" reports it, and the model allow-list matching by prefix, so an unknown id that starts with an allowed one passes as capable. The verifiers merged five duplicate groups (N3 and N7 into N1, N10 into N5, N11 into N4, N13 into N8, N15 into N14) and narrowed several findings: the two seeds do harm only once an operator runs the shown SQL, and their pages' missing step-up and client-chunk SQL reach nothing on their own; the referral cap is an operator-error amplifier for a stepped-up super-admin, and the credits offset invoices rather than pay cash; N6 holds under the AUD16-16 threat model only; the marketplace seed's oldest-family fallback fires only where the hard-coded address has no family, since in production it resolves to the owner's anchor family. The marketplace seed sits under the marketplace lane's paths, which recorded only its exposure (disputed); this lane removes it. Eight commits: the fix `0d5051527` on `audit/admin-reach-fix` from `8b35245e9`, 46 files (28 source files, 6 of them deleted: the two seed pages, their screens and their SQL modules; the seven web catalogues, each losing the 30 seed keys; 11 test files, 9 of them new); round 2 `331837562` on `audit/admin-reach-fix-r2`, 5 files (`lib/marketing/legacy-bridge.ts`, the admin marketing and content actions, 2 new test files); its re-fix `7ebf6fe94` on `audit/admin-reach-fix-r2-r1`, 2 files (`lib/marketing/platform.ts` and 1 new test file); round 3 `5fb3a933b` on `audit/admin-reach-fix-r3`, 8 files (`lib/marketing/legacy-bridge.ts`, `lib/marketing/platform.ts`, the admin marketing and platform actions, 2 new test files and one-line edits to 2 round-2 tests); round 4 `340cd7dae` on `audit/admin-reach-fix-r4`, 4 files (`lib/marketing/legacy-bridge.ts`, 1 new test file and 2 changed tests); round 5 `6c2da65e8` on `audit/admin-reach-fix-r5`, 2 files (`lib/marketing/platform.ts` and 1 new test file); round 6 `eb7281f1e` on `audit/admin-reach-fix-r6`, 2 files (`lib/marketing/platform.ts` and 1 new test file); and its re-fix `713772762` on `audit/admin-reach-fix-r6-r1`, the same 2 files. Round 6's fix `eb7281f1e` took all three; its first review closed the two RV51 items (ADMIN-R10, ADMIN-R11) and raised RV61-F5-STALES-A-CHUNK-THE-REGENERATION-RESTORES, a P2 the fix introduced, and RV61-F5-OVERLAP-SAME-TEXT-DUPLICATE, a pre-existing P3. Since round 3 the deploy no longer waits for the mirror repair: deploying first is safe, and the repair should run after this release is live, marking the unmarked mirrors, stamping the console pages made before this release, archiving the unmarked aliases at former slugs rather than marking them live, and then deleting the `unmarked` fallback (ADMIN-O11). Follow-ups from the fixers' and reviewers' non-blocking notes in rounds 3 to 6: until the repair, a rename leaves the unmarked old mirror live at `/lp/<old slug>`, as on main, which the repair's archive step clears, and a console page made before this release carries no stamp, so a legacy create or rename can take over its `/lp` path, and a first blog publish its `/blog` path, as on main; a retried `regenerate_page` or a `generate_metadata` job at the same version rewrites the page without a new version, and its `embed_page` follow-up is dropped by the idempotency key `v:<version>:embedding`, which was already so before round 5; `scripts/backfill-marketing-coverage.mjs` writes SEO and AEO with `updated_by` null, which never bumps the version, so a regeneration running at the same time can still overwrite them (0237's design, an operator script); and the narrow windows left need SQL or a lock: in `runQuestions`, a failed write back to 'answered' after the insert leaves the old path's answers published while its Retry runs at the new path (ADMIN-R11), and in `runEmbedding`, the one round trip between the page read and the existing-chunk read, and the theoretical few milliseconds between an older run's post-check read, or its existing-row read, and its stale update, which could stale a chunk a newer run just reused (ADMIN-R12, ADMIN-R13). | **CRON-01** | N1: In the automations run, one subject's refused claim, reservation, record or run_count write threw out of `runAutomations`, so every later subject and workflow was skipped for the day and the route answered 500. The row left `running` was skipped for ever, and no reaper exists anywhere. The route also had no maxDuration or budget while it sent up to 200 emails per workflow serially, so a kill mid-loop stranded the family too. | High (both verifiers: holds in full; on the `:162` path the email had already gone out and the record is what was lost; the unsent email is stranded by the kill case) | `lib/marketing/automation-runner.ts:107`, `:109`, `:124`, `:135`/`:137`, `:162` and `:174` at the base (now `STALE_RUNNING_MS` `:62`, the budget `:89` and `:112`, counted failures `:141` and `:242-262`); `app/api/cron/automations/route.ts:33-35` at the base (now maxDuration `:12`, `RUN_BUDGET_MS` `:15`, `ok` `:39`); `git grep marketing_automation_runs` finds no reaper; `tests/an-automation-subjects-failure-is-its-own.test.ts` (a refused record write fails only its own subject; the fallback stamp moves the row to failed with its receipts; a stale `running` row is re-claimed and a fresh one left alone; two passes re-claim a stale row once; the budget's unserved tail is a 502; the route declares maxDuration); 6 of 6 cases fail on the base sources (round-1 reviewer). | **Fixed:** each subject runs under its own try/catch, counted in `failures`. A refused record write gets a fenced fallback stamp to `failed` with its receipts. A `running` row older than 60 min (dated by `metadata.claimedAt`, else `created_at`) is re-claimed under `.eq('status','running').eq('metadata', <as read>)`. `budgetMs` counts the rest as `unserved`, and the route declares maxDuration 300 with a 240 s budget and answers 502 unless failures and unserved are both 0 (27e4b2648). Reviewer: a thrown `runSteps` becomes failed-attempt receipts, not a stranded row; `metadata` is not null (0020), so the JSON-null fence edge never arises. The stale comment is CRON-O5. |

Two cron runs sharing a batch, or the cron and "Sync now", both read "no mapping" and both created the event at Google or Microsoft, so the family's real calendar got two copies and the next pull imported the second as a local event. | High as reported (both verifiers: medium; the lease is warranted, but the 0018 unique constraints refuse the second mapping, so the account's sync is not broken for good and the losing run fails once) | `lib/sync/engine/generic.ts:43`, `:241` and `:254`, `app/api/cron/provider-sync/route.ts:26` and `:149`, and `app/api/sync/run/route.ts:74`, all at the base; `supabase/migrations/0018_sync_platform.sql:368-369`; new `lib/sync/account-lease.ts` (`ACCOUNT_SYNC_STALE_MS` `:54`, `claimAccountLease` `:64`, `releaseAccountLease` `:106`); now `provider-sync/route.ts:157-160` (busy) and `app/api/sync/run/route.ts:88` (409); `sync.syncAlreadyRunning` in the seven catalogues; `tests/one-sync-of-a-calendar-account-at-a-time.test.ts` (two scheduled runs sync the account once and count the second busy; "Sync now" while it is held is 409 with no second engine run; a dead holder's lease is taken over; a fresh lease is respected; a failed sync is released to the error state); 5 of 5 cases fail on the base sources (round-1 reviewer). | **Fixed:** `sync_accounts.sync_status = 'syncing'` is a compare-and-set lease (`.neq('sync_status','syncing')`), taken over after 20 min under `.lt('updated_at', cutoff)` and released fenced on `syncing`, around `runProviderSync` for the cron and "Sync now". The 0018 indexes already exist and were not added (27e4b2648). Reviewer: both callers of `runProviderSync` are leased and `sync_status` is not null. The stamp change is CRON-R5, and the Google page's entry point is CRON-R6. |

| **LIFE-01** | N1: `closeAccountAction` and `reopenAccountAction` cancelled or resumed every billable Stripe subscription and stamped or cleared `families.closed_at` behind a role check only, without the 'money' AAL2 step-up every other billing cancel path requires, so a password-only session of a parent who enrolled an authenticator could lock every member out from the paywall gate or a direct Next-Action POST. | Medium (verifiers: only families whose parent enrolled a TOTP factor; Stripe cancels at period end, so no money is lost, but the lock-out is immediate) | `app/(app)/account/actions.ts:34` (close, Stripe update `:90`, `closed_at` `:107`) and `:115` (reopen) at the base, now `needsCodeFirst` at `:36`, called at `:63` and `:146`; the sibling gates `lib/billing/route-step-up.ts:18-24` and `app/(app)/dashboard/billing/actions.ts:72-80`; the callers `components/app/close-account-card.tsx:29`, `trial-paywall-gate.tsx` and `account-closed-gate.tsx`; `tests/closing-the-account-needs-the-code.test.ts` (a password-only parent with an authenticator: Stripe and the family row untouched, told where the code goes; reopen resumes nothing; the role refusal still comes first; each of the three callers hands the refusal on; once the code is in, the close goes through from the action and the card; no code asked of a family without an authenticator); the reviewer's control: 5 cases fail. | **Fixed:** both actions run `aal2Verdict(ctx, 'money', '/dashboard/billing')` after the role check and answer `{ ok: false, error: actions.moneyNeedsYourCodeAgain, stepUp }`; the billing card, the paywall gate and the closed-account gate hand it to `reportRefusal` (9866ccb6b). Review round 1 found the step-up unreachable from behind both gates (LIFE-R1); the re-fix asks for the code inside them (fad8acb00), closed in round 2. |

## Expo mobile app and the routes that serve it — audit lane, PR #1077 — 2026-10-23

Result: **16 🛠 FIXED + PASS (16 rows; N3, N9 and N13 overlap N1 and N2 and share their fixes, and MOBILE-14 was completed by the round-1 re-fix), 1 🛠 FIXED + PASS from review round 2 (MOBILE-O5, the root typecheck), 4 🔄 IN PROGRESS (MOBILE-O1 an owner decision, which is MOBILE-06 and has no code; MOBILE-O2 the disputed item, recorded; MOBILE-O3 a review P3 for a further round; MOBILE-O4 dependency housekeeping). Merged to main as `4a1aad783` on 2026-10-23 at 00:17 UTC after a green run of all 17 checks on `e0b85f4e8`; www.bubaly.com/api/build-info served `4a1aad783` at 00:21 UTC on 2026-10-23.** The lane audited the Expo phone app under `mobile/` and the server routes it calls: the bearer path (`lib/supabase/bearer.ts`), `/api/ai`, the voice routes and `/api/calendar/occurrences`, with the tables the phone reads directly under RLS. Four lenses (authorization, record integrity, failure surfacing, external content) produced 20 candidates (5, 6, 9 and 0); each was checked by two skeptical verifiers; 17 confirmed, 1 disputed (MOBILE-O2), 2 refuted (a grocery add writing a cross-family row, which migration 0313's `list_id` trigger refuses with 42501; raw PostgREST text on the Chores and Grocery screens, which never reaches them because postgrest-js returns the error as a plain object and every catch site shows its fixed fallback). The verifiers marked N3's chore half as N1(a) and N9 as N2's root cause. Three commits: the fix `e6515c8dc` on `audit/mobile-fix` from base `a47f5ef13`, 59 files (30 source files, 5 of them new; 17 test files, 9 of them new, and the in-memory database helper; the seven web catalogues and the regenerated phone catalogue; `docs/mobile.md`; `mobile/package.json` and its lockfile); the re-fix `2123c6351` on `audit/mobile-fix-r1`, 4 files (2 source files, 1 test file, `docs/mobile.md`); and the typecheck commit `a5e7ba9a4` on `audit/mobile-fix-r2`, 1 test file. Review round 1 on `e6515c8dc` closed 14 findings and left N14 (P2), N6 (P2, the owner decision, MOBILE-O1) and N12's Today stat (P3, MOBILE-O3); round 2 on `2123c6351` closed N14, raised T1 (P1, MOBILE-O5) and kept N6 at P2. Reviewer: migrations 0374 and 0331 admit a non-manager writing done on their own open row, so the phone matches the service; the daily respawn is left to the push-scan sweep as the web's comment says, and the web's activity record has no phone equivalent (pre-existing). |

## Unauthenticated entry points — audit lane, PR #1074 — 2026-10-22

Result: **12 🛠 FIXED + PASS (12 rows; N1, N2 and N6 are one defect in the inbound-mail route and share one fix), 8 🔄 IN PROGRESS (owner items: 2 configuration, 2 decisions, 4 recorded). Merged to main as `1745c94ad` at 2026-10-22T16:54:04Z (GitHub merge identity/time independently verified in this batch). The historical lane author reported all 17 checks green on `abca6c7a3` and build-info serving `1745c94ad` at 17:00 UTC that day; those historical CI/deployment observations were not independently requalified here.** The lane audited every route and server action that answers before sign-in: the Contact Center inbound-mail webhook, the public Pay-ID and gift pages, anonymous reviews, the health route, child sign-in, the public tracking and form routes, and the money webhook. Four lenses (abuse, injection, leaks, webhooks) produced 13 candidates, none duplicates of each other; each was checked by two skeptical verifiers; 12 confirmed, 1 disputed (PUBENT-O5), 0 refuted. One fix commit, `383aca10f` on `audit/public-entry-fix` from base `665c5cc65`, 52 files; one review round on that commit closed all 12 and left two P3s (PUBENT-O7, PUBENT-O8). Each fix has a test, named per finding in the fix record. Fix-commit validation as the fixer recorded it: `tsc --noEmit -p .` exit 0; `eslint --no-ignore --max-warnings=0` on every changed TS/TSX file clean; `npm run i18n:gate` clean; vitest in UTC on 320 files (every test referencing a changed module plus all 235 source-scanning tests) in four batches, all pass; 400 further catalogue-reading tests in five batches pass (2 pre-existing expected failures); a 35-file and a 9-file rerun pass; the 23 changed or added test files (323 cases) pass in America/Los_Angeles and Asia/Tokyo; negative control: with the base commit's versions of the 19 changed source files swapped in and the new files kept, the 8 new test files all fail, 89 cases (inbound 50/57, malformed-body 14/19, health 6/8, review 4/7, pay-id 4/6, account-mirror 3/4, child-username 3/6, throttle-prune 5/5); no Playwright fixture lists a changed module, so no spec was run. The reviewer's independent run at the same commit: vitest in UTC on 323 files / 4,814 cases (23 changed or added tests, all 235 source-scanning tests, 100 tests referencing a changed module and two ratchets) in three batches (112/2,128, 110/1,269, 101/1,417), all pass; `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; eslint on all 20 changed TS/TSX sources exit 0; i18n gate clean; negative control with the `665c5cc65` versions of the 18 pre-existing changed sources (two new files kept): every one of the 8 new test files fails, 89 cases, identical to the fixer's figure. Merged tree validation (bb7c0193e = main 3f3c8de75 + the fix): `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; eslint on every changed TS/TSX file exit 0; i18n gate clean with 0 duplicate catalogue keys; all 237 source-scanning test files pass (3,402 cases); the 63 test files that are changed or name a changed module pass in UTC, America/Los_Angeles and Asia/Tokyo (1,342 cases each); no Playwright spec names a changed module.

## Calendar and hub surfaces — audit lane, PR #1073 — 2026-10-21

Result: **20 🛠 FIXED + PASS (19 rows, because N6 and N10 share one fix; plus 13 follow-up fixes: 2 from the review rounds and 11 from the follow-up round), 16 🔄 IN PROGRESS (owner items).** The lane audited the calendar module — events, recurrence and the occurrences API — and the hub surfaces: assistants, front desk, needs-you, renewals, trip intel, family health, onboarding funnel, feedback board, referrals, kitchen display, privacy export, subscription candidates, weekend discover and moving. Four lenses (authorization, record integrity, failure surfacing, external content) produced 27 candidates; the 20 most severe were each checked by two skeptical verifiers and all 20 confirmed; the other 7 were confirmed in a follow-up round. A follow-up commit `87f883212` closed the review P3s N19, N13, N15 and N6-T1 and the seven further findings U1–U7; N7-sync stays with the provider-sync lane, and the review of that commit found four minor residuals (N7-sync, N13-R1, N13-R2, N15-R1), recorded as owner rows. Each fix has a test; with every production file put back to its HEAD version and the new tests kept, each finding's tests failed, and the reviewer repeated the revert per finding and saw each test fail on an assertion, not an import error. Two review rounds on the audit fix: the first (on `0d349c2e3`) closed 15 findings and raised a regression (R1) and the assistant half of N7 as P2 blockers, N3's database half as owner action and four P3s; the second (on `ac4a1116b`) closed R1 and N7 and raised one P3 (N7-sync). Fix-commit validation as the fixer recorded it and the reviewers re-ran it: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `eslint --no-ignore --max-warnings=0` on all 50 changed TS/TSX files exit 0; `npm run i18n:gate` clean; vitest in UTC on 391 files in three batches (116 files/2,239 tests, 139/2,364, 136/1,915) for the audit fix and on 107 files (54/1,087 and 53/1,211) plus 40 ratchet and source-scan files (595 tests) for the first follow-up commit (`ac4a1116b`); the 21 changed or added test files (279 tests) pass in America/Los_Angeles and Asia/Tokyo; Playwright `routine-modal-completion` 32 passed, `local-input-unchanged-instant` with `calendar-navigation` 20 passed, and `calendar-navigation`, `bill-schedule-repair`, `finance-read-states` and `recurring-bill-payment` 57 passed; the reviewers' independent runs (154 files/3,314 tests on the audit fix; 100 files/2,163 tests and 232 source scans/3,224 tests on the first follow-up commit) all passed except `tests/node-version-is-pinned.test.ts`, which fails only because the sandbox runs Node 22 and the repo requires 24. Validation on the merged tree: not stated. Merged to main as `3f3c8de75` on 2026-10-21 at 01:15 UTC after a green run of all 17 checks on `7152af775`; www.bubaly.com/api/build-info served `3f3c8de75` at 01:18 UTC on 2026-10-21.

## Operations and intelligence dashboards — audit lane, PR #1052 — 2026-10-14

Result: **19 🛠 FIXED + PASS (plus 8 follow-up fixes from the review rounds), 16 🔄 IN PROGRESS (owner items). Merged to main as `a40c040e8` on 2026-10-14 at 15:10 UTC after a green run of all 19 checks on `a47f5ef13`; www.bubaly.com/api/build-info served `a40c040e8` at 15:13 UTC.** The lane audited the family operations and intelligence dashboards: Family Automation, the Family COO, Autonomous Family Management, Next Best Actions, Outcomes, Planning, Reasoning, Trust, the Knowledge Graph, Family Signals, the Operating Index, Family Stress, Activity, Bills due, Watchlist, Favorites, the Library, Career, Closet, Language, Scan, Customize and the App Store, with the cron jobs that compute what they show. Four lenses (authorization, record integrity, failure surfacing, external content) produced the candidates; the 20 most severe were each checked by two skeptical verifiers and 19 confirmed. Each fix has a test that drives the real page, component, action, route or service against the in-memory database; with the old source restored the fix-specific cases fail and every finding has at least one. Two review rounds on the audit fix and two follow-up rounds on what the reviewers found. Validation on the merged tree `a47f5ef13` (main plus this fix), run locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint --no-ignore --max-warnings=0` on every changed TS/TSX file clean; `npm run i18n:gate` clean with no duplicate catalogue keys; all 235 source-scanning test files, 3,274 tests pass; the 60 test files that are changed or name a changed module, 925 tests pass in each of UTC, America/Los_Angeles and Asia/Tokyo; Playwright `bill-schedule-repair` and `finance-read-states`, 36 passed; each fix commit was validated by its fixer and re-run by an independent reviewer with negative controls. No merge commit yet; live verification not applicable until merged.

## Integrations — the 80 INTEGRATION rows (every external host) — 2026-09-28

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Read on main at `7cf84171`.*

Each host was located in shipped code (`app`, `components`, `lib`, `shared`, `mobile`, `middleware.ts`, `next.config`) by a tree scan and classified by what the code does with it:
- **22 are called by the server.** Every outbound server `fetch` in `lib/`, `app/api` and `shared/` was enumerated, and every one carries a deadline, through `fetchWithDeadline`, `fetchWithTimeout` or its own signal. APNs uses HTTP/2 with its own timer.
- **No provider key reaches the browser.** The only `NEXT_PUBLIC_` values are the Supabase URL and anon key, the app and site URLs, the VAPID public key, the Stripe publishable key and build ids.
- **The rest** are CSP allow-list entries, image hosts, calendar URL patterns, share and retailer deep links, documentation links, and development sentinels.

Result: **76 ✅ PASS, 3 🛠 FIXED + PASS, 1 🔄 IN PROGRESS** (the owner's call).

| ID | Finding | Severity | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **INT-M01** | The fetcher for family-supplied URLs (calendar feeds, weekend feeds, the social-feed page reader) could be steered to an internal address by DNS rebinding. | Medium | `fetchPublicText` resolved a hostname and refused private answers, then called `fetch(hostname)`, which resolved it again. A zero-TTL answer could pass the check as public and connect as `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254`, on every redirect hop too. Recorded earlier as "Recorded, not fixed: DNS rebinding". The document fetcher already pinned its socket; this one did not. | **Fixed:** `pinnedPublicFetch` resolves, applies the same address policy, and hands the socket that exact address through `lookup`. The hostname is kept for Host and TLS, there is no pooled connection, `Accept-Encoding: identity`, and http or https. It is the default for every caller. `tests/a-public-fetch-connects-where-it-checked.test.ts` runs real sockets with a stub resolver: the rebinding second answer is refused and never connected (red on the old fetcher), the pinned address is used with the hostname in Host, and private literals are refused. |
| **INT-L01** | Two buttons opened an external site in a new tab with no `noopener`, handing it `window.opener` (reverse tabnabbing): the contacts "open in Maps" and the profile's "Rate the app". | Low | `window.open(url, '_blank')` in `components/modules/contacts-module.tsx` and `profile-module.tsx`. Links elsewhere carry `rel="noreferrer"`. | **Fixed:** both pass `'noopener,noreferrer'`. `tests/an-external-tab-gets-no-handle-back.test.ts` holds it tree-wide (red on the old tree). |
| **INT-O01** | "Rate the app" on the profile opens the App Store's front page, not a Bubaly listing. | Low | `window.open('https://apps.apple.com/', …)`; the repository holds no App Store id, so there is no listing to link. | **Owner's call:** link a listing once one exists, or change the row. ## Storage audit — five buckets through the real Storage API — 2026-09-28

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Local stack at `0463`.*

The boundary probes read `storage.objects` policies in SQL. They cannot see the three things that decide a real request: the bucket's `public` flag (served without RLS), its MIME allow-list, and the LIST endpoint. `scripts/api-audit/storage.mjs` drives the HTTP API a browser uses. It makes a parent, that parent's child, and a parent of another family, then tries every bucket as each of them and as a signed-out caller. It cleans up after itself and refuses any target but a local stack.

**Result: 54/54 OK.** The five STORAGE rows that were NOT STARTED move to ✅ PASS:
- **Where uploads may go.** Uploads land only in your own folder: `<user id>/` for `avatars`, `feedback-attachments` and `marketplace-photos`; `<family id>/` for `documents`.
- **Who else can touch an object.** Another family, the owner's own child and a signed-out caller cannot upload there, list it, overwrite it or delete from it. An HTML upload is refused by every MIME-restricted bucket.
- **`marketing-assets`** is the service role's alone.
- **`documents` and `feedback-attachments`** are private: their public URL is not served.
- **`avatars` and `marketplace-photos`** serve any object to anyone holding its URL. That exposure is declared, and their names are 122 random bits.

**Two expectations corrected on the way:**
- A public bucket also serves the object through the authenticated download API, not only the public path. That is the same exposure, not a second one, and the script records it as such.
- `marketplace-photos` keeps the shape SEC-001 closed for family media: a photo on a circle-only listing stays fetchable by anyone who kept its URL after leaving the circle. This is recorded for the owner, not changed.

**Made permanent:**
- `tests/the-audit-harness-refuses-a-non-local-target.test.ts` runs every script under `scripts/api-audit/`, plus `page-audit-session.mjs`, against a production URL and requires the refusal. It is red if any script's guard is removed.
- `family-media` (STORAGE-EA481A772907) stays with SEC-001's session.

**ROLE rows: all 61 read (49 ✅ PASS, 11 🛠 FIXED + PASS, 1 🔄 IN PROGRESS on ROLE-SCOPE-001, the owner's decision).** Each was read in full. The same-origin redirect helper was re-probed with 14 more hostile strings, and none left the origin. The local stack confirmed that an email change stays pending until confirmed, so nobody can edit their session's email onto the super-admin allowlist. The child-login throttle is backed by a per-IP limit. Every test file that names these files passes: 45 files and 686 tests for the eleven smaller modules, then 17 files and 163 tests for the next five. The billing columns on `families` and the `subscriptions` table are not writable by a parent (measured), so the trial cannot be self-extended. The last 32 (the auth pages, the auth and App Lock components, the session helpers, the mobile auth files and the operator scripts) added ROLE-L04 to -L08 below, and I18N-011, which is recorded OPEN rather than fixed because it spans 689 call sites. The App Lock is a curtain by design (`lib/security/app-lock.ts`): its salted hash is in the page and a reload resets the cooldown; the session and RLS are the boundary.

## DB-RPC pass — every function in `public`, who may call it and what it checks — 2026-09-28

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Local Supabase with every migration through `0463`.*

**What was checked.** The inventory listed 77 functions (DB-RPC-001…077). The database holds **127**, not counting extension functions, including the two added here. The 50 with no row are added as DB-RPC-078…127, and every row now carries its facts.
- **SECURITY DEFINER:** 91 functions, 62 callable and 29 triggers. **Every one pins its `search_path`.** The 36 invoker functions run with the caller's own rights; the 7 among them without a `search_path` are pure functions or triggers that read nothing outside their row.
- **Who may EXECUTE:** 16 definer functions are the service role's only. 14 are callable by `authenticated` only. 32 are callable by `anon` too, because Supabase's default privileges grant every new function to `anon` directly. Each of those reads the caller in its body, directly or through a helper, and signed-out callers are refused. The exceptions are `public_stats` and `public_handled_stats`, the marketing site's platform-wide counts, deliberately public and allowlisted by `definer-functions-check-their-caller-check.sql`.
- **Bodies read:** every callable definer function that no probe exercised. The wallet functions (`wallet_transfer`, `wallet_decide_allowance`, `wallet_decide_spend`), `move_recalculate_date`, `vacation_import_confirmation` (whose idempotent retries re-authorise), `marketplace_complete_handoff`, `marketplace_decline_offer` and `rate_limit_hit` each check the actor, the role and the family before acting.
  - `document_object_is_restricted` lets `anon` ask whether a sensitive document sits at an exact storage path. The path carries two uuids, so this is recorded, not changed.
- **Two defects found and fixed in the repository:**

## DB policy pass — every table's RLS, every policy's caller — 2026-09-28

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Local Supabase with every migration through `0461`.*

**What was checked.** For all 492 tables in `public`:
- **RLS:** enabled on every one.
- **Tables with no client policy:** 58. Every client is refused there and only the service role reaches them: the marketing, rate-limit, webhook, token and settings tables. That is the intended shape.
- **Policies:** all 1,073 permissive policies a client role can use (`anon`, `authenticated` or PUBLIC) were read. Each was judged on the expression that governs its command, `USING` for reads, updates and deletes, `WITH CHECK` for inserts. That expression names the caller in every case: `auth.uid()`/`auth.jwt()`, or a call to one of 67 public helpers whose body reaches the caller directly or through another helper (`is_family_member`, `can_manage_family`, `social_has_permission`, `is_marketplace_circle_member`, …).
- **Exceptions:** 13 policies are deliberately public: published marketing pages and Q&A, the blog, and catalogues every family shares. None sits on a table with a `family_id`. One policy is `USING (false)`, which admits nobody.

**Result: no table admits a caller it cannot identify.** A-16 (`blanket-policy-check.sql`) only forbids a literal `true`, so a policy like `using (status = 'open')` on family rows would have passed CI. This pass is the first check that would catch it.

**Made permanent:** `docs/audit/every-policy-names-its-caller-check.sql`. CI's Database job runs it, since the runner globs `*-check.sql`.
- **Derived helper set:** the caller helpers come from `pg_proc`, iterated to a fixed point, so a new helper counts the day it lands.
- **Negative control:** in a rolled-back transaction it creates a family table with a leaky `using (status = 'open')` policy and a tied one, and requires the detector to flag exactly the leaky one.
- **Allowlist checks:** it fails on a stale allowlist entry, or on an allowlisted policy that sits on family data.

**What it does not prove.** It checks that each policy names who is asking, not that the rule is the right one. For example, API-SWEEP-06 read half (a child reads the family's `transactions`) passes, because `is_family_member(family_id)` names the child. That remains the owner's decision.

**Register movement.**
- All 490 NOT STARTED DB-TBL rows move to 🔄 IN PROGRESS, each carrying its RLS state, its policy counts per command and whether it is family-scoped. What remains is per-role expectations and the workflows that use each table.
- DB-TBL-161 (`guardian_communications`), already in progress, has the result appended.
- `push_deliveries` had no row and is added as DB-TBL-492.
- Register B: **14,230 = 12,690 NOT STARTED + 1,478 IN PROGRESS + 52 FIXED + PASS + 1 PASS + 9 BLOCKED + 0 FAIL.**

**Also reconciled.** Fifteen findings in the Pass D/E/F summary tables still said OPEN although the code had fixed them: F-E02…F-E08, F-F03, F-F09, F-D01, F-D02/03 and F-G09. Each now states what the current code does and which file or migration did it. Twelve are fixed, four of those only in the repo until the operator applies their migrations. F-E02 is partial: step-up is enforced in RLS only for the budget and the vault. F-E06 is fixed as far as the repo can go.

**PRODUCTION READY: NO.**

## PUSH-007: no push notification after the first dispatch run; four nightly-job rows retested — 2026-09-28

*session_01DXw2nu25BjyRfA6Fg3YiMS. Local stack, production builds of main at `dd757a04`, then of the fix. The crons were called with a locally generated test secret.*

- **PUSH-007 (High), found by running `/api/cron/notifications` twice.** The dispatcher claims each batch with a compare-and-set on its saved cursor. It passed the cursor object to `.eq()`, which postgrest-js sends as "[object Object]", and PostgREST refused it with 22P02.

- **MAIN-F-014 → 🛠 FIXED + PASS.** 120 upcoming events were notified across two runs (a 100-per-run cap), none twice. A later run created exactly the 3 new ones, then 0.
- **MAIN-F-008 and F-011 → 🛠 FIXED + PASS.** With 1,214 families seeded, the cron reported all 1,214, paging past the 1,000-row cap.
- **MAIN-F-009 → 🛠 FIXED + PASS.** The mail provider threw on every send, and the run counted each failure and finished every family.

## DATA-023: a child's wallet page showed the newest 200 rows' sum as the balance — 2026-09-28

*session_01DXw2nu25BjyRfA6Fg3YiMS. Local stack, a production build of main at `beb2de2b`, then of the fix.*

**Found by the integrated retest of MAIN-F-F08.**
- The parent added $12.34 through the child's wallet page. The action wrote four immutable `completed` credits of 494, 494, 123 and 123 cents: the 40/40/10/10 split, conserving every cent.
- `child_wallets` has no balance column to write, so **MAIN-F-F08 → 🛠 FIXED + PASS.**
- The same page showed that teen's total as **$14**, although the ledger held $84 (the 1,200 Invest credits from the MAIN-F-J07 retest). After the top-up it showed $26.06.
- **Cause:** the page summed its history list, the newest 200 rows (`.limit(200)`). Past 200 rows, the total and every bucket were an arbitrary recent slice. At four rows per allowance or top-up, that is about a year of weekly use.
- The server re-sums before money moves, so no money was at risk. The wrong figure was the balance the parent and the child read.

**Fixed:**
- The balance is summed from a paged read of the child's whole ledger, which fails closed past its ceiling. The history list stays the newest 200, and is listed, never summed.
- `tests/a-child-wallet-balance-is-the-whole-ledger.test.ts` runs the page itself over a store capped at 1,000 rows a read. It is red on the previous code (1,386 of 8,400 invested cents).
- Retested in the browser: the parent and the teen both see $96.34, with Invest at $85.23.
- Every other place that sums the ledger (treasury, send, goals, invest, the AI wallet routes, the admin console) was checked; each already reads the whole ledger in pages.

Recorded in full as DATA-023 under High Priority. Production readiness is unchanged: **NO**.

## API sweep — every route under app/api, four callers — 2026-09-27

*Claude session_01776xJyhVe8xJQvTGeNfT9T. Register B's API rows, which no one had claimed.*

**What was run.** Every method of every `app/api/**/route.ts` (155 route methods in 147 files, discovered from disk) was called against a local production build of `main` at `25a3a808` (Next 16.3.6) and a local Supabase with every migration through `0458`. Each was called as four callers: signed out, a `child` member, a non-admin parent, and a parent who is a super admin (`scripts/api-audit/sessions.mjs`, which creates both parents through the real sign-in form and onboarding). Each call sent the input a careless or hostile client sends: nothing on a GET, and on a POST an empty JSON object and a body that is not JSON (`scripts/api-audit/sweep.mjs`, 1,008 calls). `scripts/api-audit/summarize.mjs` puts every call in one bucket:

- **FAIL**: a 5xx, a dropped connection, a stack trace or database error text in the body, an `/api/admin` route answering 2xx to a child or non-admin parent, or a cron route answering anything but 401/403 without the cron secret.
- **BLOCKED**: a 503 that says the feature is not set up on this server.
- **REVIEW**: a 2xx to a signed-out caller or to a non-JSON body.
- **OK**: everything else.

**First sweep: 24 FAIL.**
- 7 were real 500s: the four AI routes `invest`, `relationship`, `wallet` and `weekly-briefing`; billing `checkout` and `portal`; and `google/calendar/auth` with an empty body.
- The rest were honest "not configured" 503s, counted as FAIL until the summariser learned to tell them apart.
- Reading the routes behind the 500s found three more defects than the sweep could see.

**After the fixes: 0 FAIL, 30 BLOCKED, 11 REVIEW, 114 OK.**
- All 30 BLOCKED routes answer an honest 503 because this build has no AI, Stripe, push, GIF or Twilio credentials.
- All 11 REVIEW routes were read. Each is a public read-only endpoint (`health`, `build-info`, `blog/search-index`, `services/descriptions`, `exit-intent/resolve`) or reads an optional body with `readBoundedRequestJsonOrEmpty`, which treats an unreadable body as empty on purpose.
- No admin route answered a child or a non-admin parent. No cron route ran without its secret. No response carried internal detail.

| ID | Severity | Route(s) | Problem | Fix | Test (red before the fix) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-SWEEP-01 | Medium | `GET /api/google/calendar/auth` | With no Google credentials, "Connect Google" on `/dashboard/calendar` threw and left the parent on a blank 500 page. | Returns the parent to the calendar with `gcal=not_configured` and a translated toast, as the Outlook link beside it already does. | `tests/google-calendar-connect-without-credentials.test.ts` |
| API-SWEEP-02 | **High** | `POST /api/billing/{checkout,portal,cancel,change-plan}` | Super Admin → Stripe Setup saves a secret key and promises "configured value first, then env", but only checkout honoured it. Portal, cancel and change-plan read `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` alone, so a family that subscribed through the configured key could not open the portal, cancel or change plan. With no key anywhere, all four answered 500. Checkout also built its client before reading the body, so a malformed body got a 500 instead of a 400. | All four resolve the key the same way (Setup, then env). Without one they answer 503 "billing isn't set up" before any Stripe call. Checkout reads the body first. | `tests/billing-uses-the-stripe-keys-the-admin-configured.test.ts` (8 of 10 cases red before) |
| API-SWEEP-03 | **High** | `POST /api/webhooks/stripe` | Read `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` alone and built a client with `getStripe()` just to check the signature. On a deployment whose key and secret live in Stripe Setup, that threw, and the catch answered "signature invalid" to every real event, so no subscription would ever be recorded. | The Setup secret first, then env, verified with Stripe's keyless static verifier (`constructWebhookEvent` in `lib/stripe.ts`). A wrong secret is still refused. | Same file, with real signatures from Stripe's own test-header generator |
| API-SWEEP-04 | Medium | 14 AI routes; `ai/health/coach` | With no AI key, 18 AI routes said "the engine isn't set up" (503). Nine let the provider's throw reach a generic catch (500). Four answered 502 "temporarily unavailable", which tells the family to retry when retrying cannot work. `ai/health/coach` checked only the environment, so a key saved in Admin → AI Engine was reported missing. | Each asks `isAIConfigured()` before calling the provider. Three routes keep their deliberate model-free fallback, named in the guard: `journal`, `savings` and `behavior/insight`. | `tests/an-ai-route-says-when-the-engine-is-not-set-up.test.ts` (15 of 31 red before) |
| API-SWEEP-05 | **High** (privacy) | `POST /api/ai/savings` | Answered a signed-in child with advice built from the family's transactions, budgets, unpaid bills and subscriptions. The finance service refuses non-managers ("Family finances are private to the adults in this family"), and the privacy export withholds `finances` from a child. | 403 for non-managers before any read. | `tests/a-child-is-not-given-the-familys-savings-advice.test.ts` (3 of 5 red before) |
| API-SWEEP-07 | Medium | invite, welcome, referral and admin re-send; `cron/weekly-digest`, `cron/chore-reminders` | Found by the cron pass (below): `weekly-digest` reported `{"sent":4}` on a server with no mail provider. `sendEmail`/`sendReactEmail` answer `{ ok: true, skipped: true }` without `RESEND_API_KEY`, a contract the contact form relies on. So every caller that read only `ok` called nothing sent "sent". The invite, welcome, referral and admin re-send flows told the person their email had gone. The two crons counted every skip as a send. (The notification digest was already safe: it stops before sending when email is off.) | Each caller reads `skipped`. The four person-facing flows answer their existing "couldn't send" message (the referral also rolls back its record). The crons count a skip as a skip. | `tests/an-email-that-was-not-sent-is-not-reported-sent.test.ts` (8 callers red before); `tests/an-invite-with-no-mail-provider-is-not-sent.test.ts` (the real `lib/email`, red before) |
| API-SWEEP-06 | **High** (privacy) — ⚠️ **OPEN (reads)**; writes 🛠 FIXED + PASS (0460) | database: `transactions`, `budgets`, `bills`, `subscriptions_tracked` | Found while tracing API-SWEEP-05. Probed with a child's own session against the local database: each table's SELECT policy is `is_family_member(family_id)`, so a child reads the family's budgets, bills and tracked subscriptions straight from the REST API. `subscriptions_tracked` also lets any member *write* (`Members manage subscriptions_tracked`, command `*`). Migration 0267 guards only the writes on the first three. The app treats finances as adults-only in three places, and the database does not. | **Write half fixed** (session_01TRY21ZKsFrfB3qtoP972A4, 2026-09-28): `0460_a_child_cannot_rewrite_the_familys_subscriptions.sql` drops 0076's `FOR ALL` "Members manage subscriptions_tracked" and makes insert, update and delete `can_manage_family`, the 0267 shape; reads stay `is_family_member`. Page audit B11 had watched a PIN child add a family subscription. Checked on the local stack as that child: "Add subscription" answers "You don't have permission to do that…" and writes nothing, and the parent's add still says "Added". Needs the operator's production migration step like every schema change (PROD-DB-0177). **Read half not fixed.** A manager-only SELECT policy is the obvious fix, but the home page, wallet hub, voting, briefing and agent readers also read these tables. It needs the owner's decision on what a child may see, then a migration, then those readers checked. Production application of any migration is the owner's (PROD-DB-0177). | Writes: `docs/audit/a-child-cannot-rewrite-the-familys-subscriptions-check.sql`. It runs as a real child session, with a negative control (the same child makes all four writes in a household they manage) and a check on the whole policy set. It fails before 0460 on both the policy check and "1: a child added a family subscription", and passes after. Reads: a probe asserting a child JWT reads zero rows, still to write when the owner decides |
| API-SWEEP-08 | Medium | `POST /api/email/invite` | Found by session_01KP9rt5rVQ9jDMpZp2xBy3K while retesting API-SWEEP-07's invite change on a local stack. `rate_limit_hit` (0179) raises when a signed-in caller's key does not name their own user id. This route keyed its bucket `email:invite:<familyId>` and evaluated it on the member's session client, so the RPC raised, the limiter failed closed, and every invite email answered 429. The invite form said, every time, that it could not send the invitation. | The family-wide bound is the route's stated intent and is kept. It is now evaluated on the service client, as every IP- and address-keyed public route already is. The invite read stays on the member's session. Retested live on a production build against a real invite row: the request passed the limiter, wrote the bucket (count 1) and reached the send, while the earlier builds answered 429. | `tests/a-signed-in-rate-limit-key-names-the-caller.test.ts` checks all 86 rate-limit calls in `app/` and `lib/`: any key not provably on the service client must name the caller. It flags exactly this route on the old code. |

**Cron pass.** Each of the 27 jobs in `vercel.json` was run on the same build:
- **Without the secret:** every one answered 401.
- **With `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET`:** every one answered 200 within a second, reporting zero failures, over the local database's nine families.

`/api/cron/library-feeds` is scheduled but had no JOB row, so it is added. The JOB rows move to 🔄 IN PROGRESS. What remains for them is a run over populated data, provider delivery, and the deployed scheduler, which cannot run in production until the owner sets `CRON_SECRET` (PROD-ENV).

**What each API row now says.** Register B's 142 NOT STARTED API rows move to 🔄 IN PROGRESS, not PASS. Each row records:
- the sweep's per-caller statuses;
- its verdict;
- the fix where there was one;
- "Remaining: a valid request, its database side effects and response shape, end to end".

The eleven rows other sessions already had in progress keep their text, with the sweep's result appended. Two routes on disk had no row (`GET /api/blog/search-index`, `GET /api/cron/library-feeds`); they are added as API-9158428527C6 and API-9DB7C4EE8804. Register B after both passes: **14,229 items: 13,663 NOT STARTED, 551 IN PROGRESS, 10 FIXED + PASS, 4 BLOCKED, 1 FAIL.** No closure is claimed.

## Page Audit — every page on www.bubaly.com

*Started 2026-09-27 on the owner's instruction: "go through every single page
on bubaly.com and audit to make sure each is working perfectly, with no
issues … allow other bots (Claude and Codex) to work simultaneously on this.
Make sure to fix everything uncovered before moving on."*

**What a row's status means, exactly.** This is a *page* audit, not a workflow
audit: ✅ CLEAN says the page renders correctly, not that every action on it has
been exercised end to end. That is why no `PAGE-` or `UI-ROUTE-` row above is
moved to PASS from here — those registers mean a full workflow verified, and
this section links to them instead of overwriting them.

A page is ✅ **CLEAN** when all three hold:

- **Signed out, production** (`scripts/page-audit/crawl.mjs` against
  https://www.bubaly.com, phone 375×812 and desktop 1280×800): the right answer
  for a visitor — the page itself for a public route, a redirect to `/login`
  for a signed-in one, a 404 for a dynamic route opened with an id that matches
  nothing — with no uncaught error, no console error, no failed or 4xx/5xx
  subresource, no horizontal overflow, and no axe WCAG 2.1 A/AA *serious* or
  *critical* violation. Every link found on a crawled page is also requested.
- **Signed in, local sweep** (`tests/e2e/every-page-signed-in.spec.ts`, run in
  CI's E2E job against the disposable Supabase; locally the same against
  `supabase start`): opened by a parent who is also a super admin, the page
  answers below 500 and not 404 (a dynamic route may 404 on its no-such-id
  path), throws nothing, logs no console error, renders no raw catalogue key,
  does not double the brand in its title and does not overflow 1280 px. The
  spec discovers routes from `app/**/page.tsx`, so a page added tomorrow is in
  it tomorrow.
- **Signed in, phone** (`scripts/page-audit/crawl.mjs` with `STORAGE_STATE`
  set to that signed-in session, 375×812, against the same local build): the
  signed-out crawl's checks — axe WCAG 2.1 A/AA *serious*/*critical*,
  overflow, uncaught and console errors, failed subresources — on the page a
  parent actually sees on a phone. Added after the desktop-only sweep had
  called 340 pages clean: at phone width every signed-in page failed axe on
  the shell (a nameless logo link, avatar initials at 4.46:1), and 55 pages
  had their own failures. A page is not clean until all three checks hold.

Other statuses: 🔧 **FIXED, NOT LIVE** (the defect is fixed in a named commit
that production does not serve yet), 🔧 **FIXED, LIVE — re-crawl pending**
(production serves the fix; the signed-out production crawl has not been
re-run on it, so the row is not yet called clean), ⚠️ **OPEN** (a defect is recorded and
not fixed, with the reason), 🔒 **OWNER** (the fix is the owner's — data, a
secret, a decision), 🔄 **CLAIMED** (someone is on it; see Claim).

### Working on this in parallel (Claude, Codex, anyone)

The 398 routes are split into six **lanes**. A lane is claimed as a whole, so
two sessions never edit neighbouring rows and their merges do not conflict.

1. `git fetch origin main` and read the **Lanes** table *on origin/main*, and
   the open PRs touching `finalaudit.md`. Take a lane whose Claim is empty or
   older than 12 hours.
2. Put your session id and the UTC time in that lane's Claim cell, commit that
   one line alone, and get it to `main` first (a claim nobody else can see is
   not a claim).
3. Work your lane's rows only: re-run the two checks for the rows you touch,
   fix what you find (the same rules as the rest of this audit — a failing test
   first, the fix, the test green, mutation-proved where it can be), update the
   row, and move it to 🔧 FIXED, NOT LIVE with the commit. After the release
   reaches production, re-crawl the route and move it to ✅ CLEAN.
4. Release the lane (clear the Claim) when you stop, finished or not.

Re-running the checks: `node scripts/page-audit/routes.mjs > paths.txt`, then
`node scripts/page-audit/crawl.mjs paths.txt out.jsonl 4` and
`python3 scripts/page-audit/summarize.py out.jsonl`; and
`E2E_AUTHENTICATED=1 npx playwright test tests/e2e/every-page-signed-in.spec.ts --project=chromium`
with the local Supabase credentials in the environment; and, for the phone
column, `STORAGE_STATE=state.json BASE=http://localhost:3107 VIEWPORTS=phone
node scripts/page-audit/crawl.mjs paths.txt out.jsonl 4` with a storage state
saved from a signed-in browser.
